I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to use the full year, and I trust it because I know how to manage it and it gives steady grain for sale and for home needs. I will stay with mostly improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, because I want stable yield more than taking chances on something unfamiliar. For wheat, I will focus on water and fertilizer at the key stages, and I will spray only when disease, aphids, or weeds are likely to cut yield. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize, using no-tillage so I do not lose time or soil moisture. I will put more nitrogen on maize because it responds well, give a couple of irrigations if water is available, and control weeds and insects early so the crop can hold a good stand through summer. I am choosing this plan because it fits my land, my experience, the local weather, and the need to reduce risk.
